summary: The extraction is sound for PR preparation. The checked-out gpu_input_group.py, gpu_input_window.py, gpu_events.py hunk and both unit-test files match the supplied diff line for line, and the target's later borrowed/owned accounting, field-access and IPC code is untouched by these files. Pool ownership contracts hold on inspection: only the BD thread mutates _groups/_busy_slots/_candidates; the consumer-side callback only does SimpleQueue.put; eligibility (closed and unreferenced) is separate from CUDA completion (window.poll still gates _forget); a failed window.poll or release_raw leaves the state in _groups and _candidates for retry; slots and small credits are released only in _forget after release_raw succeeds; stale notifications are rejected by `self._groups.get(state.key) is state`; and a partial issue_groups failure leaves started reads in _groups with busy slots for close() to drain, while the reader's own issue_group/issue_batch handles its internal drain. No change to physical read counts/sizes, stream scheduling, or reader pending-list scans. The CHANGELOG, performance doc and PR body are honest: they attribute the 1.27 to 2.18 GiB/s, 50,101 to 101 poll and 31 native-test results to the original research implementation, state that the PR base has not been rerun on GPU or rebenchmarked, and claim only the 1,023-test CPU pass on this tree. Three low, non-blocking items are recorded (stale "review pending" line, fork-link reachability before publication, and a documented partial-failure behaviour that is a faithful port and out of redesign scope). No new-base GPU acceptance is asserted or inferred.
checks: Read full psana/psana/gpu/gpu_input_group.py at checkout; content equals supplied diff (busy-slot set, SimpleQueue retirement queue, issue_groups validation-before-I/O, _issue_reserved, _collect_candidates identity check, candidate-only poll, _forget order release_raw -> groups -> busy -> candidates -> small, close() discarding stale notifications).

Read full psana/psana/gpu/gpu_input_window.py; notify_when_retirable registers once under the RLock, fires only when closed and unreferenced, is cleared after firing, and _try_retire calls _notify_retirable before the released/closed checks; CUDA event checks unchanged.

Read gpu_events.py _issue_group_reads (lines 888-917) and surrounding _issue_gpu_read/_wait_gpu_read/_drain_pending_gpu_read/_close_resources; controller change limited to replacing the per-group issue loop with issue_groups and the documented partial-failure comment; pool.close() is still called from _close_resources.

Read both test files in full; the seven new tests cover plan reuse without repolling, pre-I/O conflict rejection, partial submission ownership, live-window skipping with delayed CUDA retry, consumer-thread enqueue plus stale-notification rejection, release_raw failure preserving candidate/busy slot, and failed notification registration not binding the window.

Grepped psana for all uses of _busy_slots, _candidates, _retirement_queue, issue_groups, notify_when_retirable, plan_slots, .issue( and _pending_gpu_read; only test_gpu_slot_selection.py fakes pool internals and it was updated to seed/discard _busy_slots consistently.
Verified gpu_kvikio_read.issue_group (lines 248-291) still performs budget check and _check_slot_available before _submit_read, so issue_groups' pre-validation does not bypass reader-level guards.
Confirmed design.md contains no stale 'poll all groups' description; module docstring updated to 'Only unreferenced windows enter the retirement queue'.
Confirmed the checkout has no .github PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE and no prior root CHANGELOG.md; the new CHANGELOG.md has a single Unreleased/Fixed entry with no unrelated history.

Reviewed PR body and performance doc for honesty: native GPU and benchmark numbers attributed to the research branch/original implementation; explicit statement that the PR-base runtime has not been rerun on GPU or rebenchmarked; CPU count 1,023 matches supplied log; no issue closure asserted; checklist items for Actions and Fix #XXX left unchecked.
Cross-checked supplied CPU test log: 1023 passed in 10.19s with no failures or skips reported.

findings.evidence: If issue_groups raises mid-plan on a non-poisoning allocation failure (reader.issue_group GpuMemoryPressureError after earlier groups submitted), _pending_gpu_read is the empty list, so the pressure retry at line 1013 raises 'a pre-issued GPU read is already outstanding' and started reads are read only by pool.close(). The pre-port loop also left _pending_gpu_read non-None, so retry behaviour is unchanged; only the drain location moved from _drain_pending_gpu_read to pool.close(), as the in-code comment states.
findings.requested_change: No code change requested (faithful port of the reviewed implementation; redesign out of scope). Optionally mention in the PR body that partial-plan failures are drained by the pool at close, so upstream reviewers see the intended ownership path.
